# Rejection patterns in closed PRs: pingdotgg/t3code, 2026-04-25 to 2026-10-25

Scope: every closed PR in `pingdotgg/t3code` with closedAt from 2026-04-25 through 2026-10-25, fetched in monthly windows (split where a window hit the 500-result cap). UI-relevant = title or label matches the brief's keyword list (word-start match; `ui`, `ux`, `ios`, `tab`, `diff` matched as whole words). Discussion was read for the 100 most recently closed unmerged UI PRs (closed 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-25). Raw JSON is in `/tmp/t3code-pa-closed/`.

## Summary numbers

| Set                                                    |  Total | Merged | Unmerged |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -----: | -----: | -------: |
| All closed PRs (2026-04-25 to 2026-10-25)              | 10,092 |  6,550 |    3,542 |
| UI-relevant by keyword (title or label)                |  4,298 |  2,858 |    1,440 |
| Unmerged UI PRs with discussion read (100 most recent) |    100 |      0 |      100 |

- Merged UI PRs are 43.6% of all merged PRs, so the keyword filter is broad. The largest keyword hit counts are `mobile` (1,081), `desktop` (563), and `composer` (399).
- Merge rate by contributor status, all closed PRs: `trusted` (vouched) 85.6% (5,130/5,991); `unvouched` 34.6% (1,414/4,090). For UI-relevant PRs: `trusted` 85.7%, `unvouched` 37.3%.
- Merge rate by size label, all closed PRs: XS 82.4%, S 75.8%, M 70.7%, L 58.3%, XL 55.1%, XXL 38.1%.
- Merge rate by size label, `unvouched` only: XS 68.6%, S 54.6%, M 41.8%, L 16.3%, XL 5.7%, XXL 3.7%.
- Image or video in PR body: 1,562/2,858 merged UI PRs (54.7%) vs 711/1,440 unmerged UI PRs (49.4%).

What the merged UI PRs have in common:

- Size: median 106 changed lines (p75 311, p90 933); the unmerged UI set has median 255 (p90 2621). By label: `size:M` 751, `size:L` 681, `size:XS` 549, `size:S` 518, `size:XXL` 183, `size:XL` 174, `size:none` 2 (median by lines is the figure above).
- Who: 2,219 of 2,858 merged UI PRs (77.6%) came from vouched (`trusted`) contributors. `juliusmarminge` authored 1,133 and was the merger on 1,880. Only 638 were from `unvouched` authors.
- Shape: of the 638 merged PRs from `unvouched` authors, 543 (85.1%) had a `fix(...)` title and 555 (87.0%) were `size:XS`, `size:S` or `size:M`.
- Speed: median 0.2 days open (about 5 hours), p90 8.6 days. The fast median is consistent with maintainer-authored or maintainer-completed work (takeovers and replacement PRs); this is an inference from timing, not a recorded fact.
- Evidence: only 1,562 of 2,858 merged UI PR bodies (54.7%) contained an image or video, against 49.4% of unmerged ones. Screenshots were not what separated merged from unmerged; the closing comments cited the quality and completeness of the evidence instead.

## Rules for our PRs

Each rule is derived from the counts above. Merge rates are closed-PR merge rates over 2026-04-25 to 2026-10-25.

1. Expect the contributor-status gate to decide most outcomes. Unvouched UI PRs merged 37.3% of the time versus 85.7% for vouched ones. Plan as an unvouched contributor: a change outside a focused bug fix is likely to be closed or deferred.
2. Keep the diff at XS or S. Unvouched closed PRs merged 68.6% at XS, 54.6% at S, 41.8% at M, 16.3% at L, and 5.7% at XL (XXL 3.7%). Split anything above M.
3. Frame UI work as a defect fix with a repro, not a feature or redesign. Unvouched UI PRs titled `fix(...)` merged 50.2%; those titled `feat(...)` merged 9.9%. Of the 100 closures, 10 lacked prior approval and 21 were stale or closed by their author.
4. Get prior approval before any setting, default, new workflow, or layout change. Unvouched UI PRs with `settings` in the title merged 28.9% versus 89.8% for vouched ones. Settings are accepted only as a focused option for an existing capability, with the approval linked in the PR (CONTRIBUTING's configuration route).
5. One underlying problem per PR. 2 closures cited the one-problem rule outright, and a PR combining a perf fix with a cleanup was split by the maintainers. Keep one defect per PR and move any refactor or cleanup to its own PR.
6. Attach before/after screenshots for every UI change, plus a short recording for motion, focus, keyboard, or timing. 10 of the 100 closures cited missing or inadequate UI verification, and several were closed where the verification section said screenshots were declined. Media was not the separator: 54.7% of merged and 49.4% of unmerged UI PR bodies contained an image or video, so the stated evidence and completeness mattered more than presence.
7. Test on the platform you touch, and say so. Unvouched mobile UI PRs (titles matching mobile, Android, or iOS) merged 43.4%. Closures quoted "no app build or device screenshots were checked" and "not built or tested on Android".
8. Check for overlap, then rebase on main just before you open. 28 of the 100 closures (9 superseded by a maintainer change or takeover, 19 duplicate or landed elsewhere) were closed because the same fix had merged, was in flight, or was taken over by a maintainer.
9. State the model and harness in the PR description, and never use Gemini or Muse models other than Muse Wonder Full. 20 of the 100 closures were model-policy closures. 19 were cleanup notes from a maintainer agent for PRs that named no model or an older one, asking for a rebuild with a current model. One closure cited code written by a Muse model.
10. Open against the correct repository. 5 of the 100 were opened upstream by mistake or belonged in a fork.
11. Match approved scope and intended product behavior. 3 of the 100 closures were design or intended-behavior disagreements, such as a change that made close buttons permanently visible when the approved scope kept them hover-revealed.
12. Expect the Macroscope gate to flag breadth. Of the 100 PRs, 52 got an "Approved" or "Would Approve" verdict and 25 "Not approved", with 13 "Needs Human Approval". Of the 52 positive verdicts, 47 were on XS, S, or M PRs and 0 on XL or XXL. The negative verdicts cited breadth and behavior change, not only correctness.

## Who decides

- Triage exemptions (logins whose PRs bypass triage, from `.github/TRIAGE_EXEMPTIONS.td`): `juliusmarminge`, `t3dotgg`, `maria-rcks`, `bmdavis419`, `markflorkowski`, `Yash-Singh1`.
- Collaborator without a triage exemption: `shivamhwp` (`COLLABORATOR` association). Closed 2 of the 100 and was `mergedBy` on 79 merged UI PRs.
- Closing actor for the 100 read PRs, from the last `closed` event: `maria-rcks` 28, `juliusmarminge` 29, `t3dotgg` 7, `shivamhwp` 2. 38 were closed by their own author, including some maintainers' own PRs. One had no recorded closer.
- Merger for the 2,858 merged UI PRs (GraphQL `mergedBy`): `juliusmarminge` 1,880, `maria-rcks` 469, `t3dotgg` 324, `Yash-Singh1` 96, `shivamhwp` 79, and a few others.
- Automated, from `.github/workflows` and `.github/triage` in the checkout:
  - `pr-vouch.yml` applies `vouch:trusted` or `vouch:unvouched` from `.github/VOUCHED.td`. These are labels, not eligibility rules.
  - `pr-size.yml` applies `size:*`: XS 0-9, S 10-29, M 30-99, L 100-499, XL 500-999, XXL 1,000+ effective changed lines (test files excluded in mixed PRs).
  - The `contribution-triage` skill (`.claude/skills/contribution-triage`) checks problem, approval, scope, evidence, and model, and closes ineligible PRs with a rule citation. The maintainer-run notes in the closures ("This comment is posted by Julius' dot", "Grok responding on behalf of Julius", "Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Theo", "Written by `claude-opus-5-5` on behalf of Maria") are AI-written replies posted under maintainer names; they carry the closing reasons.
  - `macroscopeapp[bot]` posts the Approvability verdict (Approved, Would Approve, Needs Human Approval, Not approved). The `macroscope-review` label is applied to PRs handed to Macroscope review (per the contribution-triage skill). Neither a verdict nor the label merges a PR.
  - `coderabbitai[bot]`, `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, and `cursor[bot]` leave review comments and are not closers.
  - `github-actions[bot]` posts a thread-transfer impact report on some PRs.
- Stock closing lines seen in the 100: "Closing under the one-problem rule", "Closing under the prior-approval rule", "Closing for missing UI verification", and "We are cleaning up open PRs, and this one does not say which model or harness was used".

## Incomplete

- Only 100 of the 1,440 unmerged UI PRs were read, as the brief specified. The other 1,340 rows of Table 3 are marked `not read` and have no category or quote. The 100 are the most recently closed (2026-10-11 to 2026-10-25), so Table 1 describes that recent window, not all six months.
- Categories (j) wrong layer and (k) performance concern had no matches among the 100.
- The UI keyword filter is mechanical (title or label, word-start match). It is broad: the largest hit counts are `mobile` (1,081), `desktop` (563), `composer` (399), `sidebar` (360), and `settings` (302), and some hits are backend or CI work. Tables 2 and 3 are a superset of UI work.
- Image or video detection is a regex on the PR body only. It does not check comments or reviews, or the quality of the evidence.
- `days open` uses createdAt to closedAt from GraphQL, which can differ from merge time for a few PRs.
- Policy discrepancy: closure comments on 16763 and 17575 cite a "500-line review limit for unvouched contributors" and "focused bug fixes" only. The `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the local checkout says "There is no line-count or file-count cutoff" and calls focused bug fixes "most likely" accepted, not exclusive. I did not establish which version applied when these PRs were closed.
- Roles for `Yash-Singh1`, `markflorkowski`, and `bmdavis419` come from the exemption file only. The collaborator-permission API returned 403, so their repository permission was not verified.
- Saved comments were truncated to 700 characters, as specified. Quotes are at most 200 characters and come from those truncated bodies, so a longer maintainer explanation may be cut.
- 10 of the 100 PRs had no Macroscope verdict in the saved comments, so the verdict counts in the Table 1 notes cover only the rest.
- Closing actors come from each PR's `closed` events (last event). A PR closed, reopened, and closed again is attributed to its final closer.
